Fresh third-party data on Muse, the AI agent from Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), is lifting shares of the social media giant and splitting its category. Meta Platforms stock is at $744.72, up 4% in afternoon trading. Meanwhile, Snap Inc. (NYSE:SNAP) shares are at $6.45, up 3%, a gain just shy of Meta Platforms'.

Fritz Jorgensen / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

At the same time, Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) stock trades at $155.23, down 3%, moving against both of its advertising-driven peers. Reddit stock is down 32% so far this year.

For broad-market context, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is at $777.88, down 0.1%. The Global X Social Media ETF (NASDAQ:SOCL) is at $44.18, down 0.7%, slipping even as Meta Platforms stock rises.

Muse Retention Data Lifts Meta

Analysis from Sensor Tower found that Muse brings back 73% of new users the day after they install it. That early rate tops the comparable figure for OpenAI's ChatGPT, although ChatGPT pulls ahead between the eighth and ninth day. Separate data from Similarweb put Muse daily active users at 2.182 million on October 5, with usage rising through the month.

Reddit has seen a sharp reset this year, with the share price down 33.9% year to date. This raises the question for investors of whether that slide now lines up with what the company is actually earning.

The year to date decline of 33.9% puts Reddit's valuation under a spotlight, because the move reshapes how much investors are effectively paying for each dollar of current and expected earnings.

Recent wins with advertisers and the new partnership with Zefr can influence how investors think about Reddit's future profit potential, since stronger ad demand and better brand controls may support earnings quality over time.

Your read on Reddit is one view; the desks covering it have another. See what analysts think Reddit's shares could be worth.

For investors, the debate is whether Reddit's current share price is adequately supported by the earnings the business is producing today and is realistically expected to produce in the future.

If this reset in Reddit's valuation has you rethinking what you pay for earnings, it can help to compare that same question across 29 high quality undervalued stocks

Is Reddit Getting Expensive on Earnings?

The P/E ratio works reasonably well for Reddit because profit is now part of the picture and investors often anchor expectations to what each dollar of earnings costs. On that score, the stock trades on roughly 35.3x earnings, which is higher than the peer average of about 30.2x and far above the wider Interactive Media and Services sector on roughly 11.1x. That mix of comparisons suggests Reddit is being treated more like a premium internet platform rather than a typical industry incumbent.

Because the current P/E sits above the level suggested by a tailored fair multiple that factors in Reddit's economics and risk profile, the shares screen as overvalued on this yardstick. The recent gains in advertiser budgets and the Zefr partnership help explain why the market is willing to pay a higher price, yet the multiple already reflects a generous view of what that kind of momentum could mean for future profitability. Reddit (RDDT) Stock Is Up, What You Need To Know
What Happened?

Shares of online community and discussion platform Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) jumped 3.3% in the pre-market session as markets took a breather following an AI driven sell-off in the previous session.

Also, Needham analyst Laura Martin reiterated a Buy rating and a $300.00 price target on the company, citing traffic tracker findings that pointed to bullish third-quarter 2026 user and revenue growth.

The analysis highlighted that web traffic data signaled positive momentum in both audience expansion and revenue for the third quarter of 2026. Needham's maintained $300.00 price target reflects sustained confidence in the company's long-term business trajectory. For digital media platforms, third-party traffic measurements often serve as an early indicator of user engagement, which directly affects advertising demand and financial performance. Market participants appeared encouraged by indications that platform activity remains robust heading into the quarterly report.

Technology shares rebounded in the morning after the previous session's retreat sparked by an underwhelming revenue update from OpenAI, according to CNBC.The quick rebound reflects an improved appetite to treat OpenAI's revenue shortfall as an isolated valuation reset for frontier model labs rather than an impairment of physical computing buildouts, drawing capital back toward bottleneck hardware and data center capacity.

After the initial pop, the shares cooled down to $160.86, up 2.8% from the previous close.

Is now the time to buy Reddit? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What Is The Market Telling Us

Reddit's shares are extremely volatile and have had 59 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 11 days ago when the stock dropped 3.8% on the news that the benchmark U.S. 10-year Treasury yield climbed back above 5% to levels not seen since 2007, lifting discount rates on long-duration growth earnings.

According to CNBC, the 10-year yield surged to 5.23% on Friday, its highest level since 2007, after trading below 4.8% earlier in September. CNBC reported Monday that the yield was again pressing multiyear highs — above 5.23% in morning trade — as oil stayed elevated and investors braced for PCE, GDP, and jobs data. Macquarie strategist Thierry Wizman told CNBC the move reflects not only sticky inflation and Fed hike odds, but also heavy Treasury and corporate bond issuance, including AI-related borrowing.
